title: Resolving modern endpoint problems with AI
summary: Use AI assistants and Copilot in Intune to diagnose real endpoint problems: enrollment failures, sync and compliance issues, app install errors, and cryptic error codes, by gathering signal, feeding structured context to AI, and validating every hypothesis against the portal and Microsoft Learn.
objectives: Gather the right diagnostic signal before asking AI: error codes, logs, Event Viewer, and IntuneManagementExtension logs
Feed structured context to an AI assistant and ask for ranked hypotheses and the next diagnostic step
Use Copilot in Intune to query a device's real compliance, sync, and policy state
Diagnose common modern endpoint issues: enrollment failures, sync stalls, compliance going red, and app install failures
Interpret error codes (such as 0x8018-style hash codes) with AI as a starting point
Validate AI hypotheses against the portal and official docs before acting, knowing AI can invent error-code meanings

quiz.q: What should you do BEFORE asking an AI assistant to diagnose an endpoint issue?
options: Gather concrete signal: error codes, logs, and the device's state
Ask the user to buy a new laptop
quiz.why: AI is only as good as the context you give it. Gathering error codes, logs, and the actual device state lets the AI produce useful, grounded hypotheses instead of generic guesses.

quiz.q: On Windows, which log is the key place to look for Intune app and script (Win32/PowerShell) deployment failures?
quiz.why: The Intune Management Extension (IME) handles Win32 app and PowerShell script delivery, and its log (IntuneManagementExtension.log) records the detailed success/failure detail you feed to AI.

quiz.q: An AI confidently tells you that error code 0x80180014 means a specific thing. What is the correct next move?
options: Trust it and tell the user that's the cause
Validate the code against official Microsoft documentation before acting
quiz.why: AI can invent or misremember error-code meanings. Always validate the code against official Microsoft Learn docs and the portal before you act on it.

quiz.q: How can Copilot in Intune help diagnose a device showing as non-compliant?
options: It answers in natural language using your tenant's real device and policy data
It can only show marketing material
quiz.why: Copilot in Intune is grounded in your tenant's actual data, so it can explain in plain language why a specific device is non-compliant and which policies apply.

quiz.q: Name one source of diagnostic signal you can collect from a Windows endpoint before involving AI.
quiz.answer: Event Viewer logs, the IntuneManagementExtension log, the exact error code, or the device's compliance and sync status in Intune.
quiz.why: Concrete signal grounds the AI's hypotheses; without it the AI only guesses generically.

quiz.q: In one sentence, what role does AI play in endpoint diagnosis, and what role does it NOT play?
quiz.answer: AI gives you ranked hypotheses and next steps to investigate, but it does not give verified truth; you confirm everything in the portal and logs.
quiz.why: AI accelerates the investigation by suggesting where to look, but the human validates each hypothesis against real evidence.

body_markdown:
## The diagnostic loop

Modern endpoint problems are rarely solved by guessing. The reliable pattern is a loop: **gather signal**, **feed structured context to AI**, **ask for ranked hypotheses and the next step**, then **validate** against the portal and Microsoft Learn. AI is a thinking partner that points you at likely causes fast — it is not the source of truth. You are.

## Step 1: gather the signal

AI is only as good as the context you give it. Before you prompt anything, collect concrete evidence. On a Windows endpoint that means:

```text
- The exact error code (e.g. 0x80180014-style hex codes)
- Event Viewer: Applications and Services Logs >
  Microsoft > Windows > DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics
- The IntuneManagementExtension log (for Win32 apps + PS scripts):
  C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs
- The device's compliance, sync, and policy state in Intune
```

A vague "it won't enroll" becomes a solvable problem the moment you have the error code and the relevant log lines.

## Step 2: feed structured context to AI

Give the AI the facts, then ask for *ranked hypotheses* and the single next diagnostic step — not a magic fix.

```text
A Windows 11 device fails Intune enrollment with error 0x80180014.
Context: Entra hybrid-joined, user is licensed, MDM auto-enrollment
is configured. Give me the 4 most likely causes ranked by
probability, the one log or setting to check for each, and the
first diagnostic step. Note any cause you are unsure about.
```

That "note any cause you are unsure about" line is gold — it nudges the model to flag its own uncertainty.

## Step 3: use Copilot in Intune for real device state

For anything tenant-specific, **Copilot in Intune** beats a public chatbot because it reads your real data.

```text
1. Go to https://intune.microsoft.com
2. Devices > pick the affected device
3. Open the Copilot pane and ask:
   "Why is this device non-compliant and what policy is failing?"
   "When did this device last check in, and is it syncing?"
```

## Common problems AI helps with

- **Enrollment failures** — licensing, auto-enrollment scope, device limits, or hybrid-join trust issues.
- **Sync / check-in stalls** — the device hasn't talked to Intune; policies look 'not applied' because nothing has run yet.
- **Compliance gone red** — a single setting (BitLocker, Defender, OS version) flipped the device non-compliant, which can then trigger a **Conditional Access** lockout.
- **App install failures** — Win32 app detection rules, dependencies, or requirement rules; the IME log holds the real reason.
- **BitLocker / Conditional Access lockouts** — escalate carefully; AI helps you read the policy chain, but never bypass security controls on a hunch.

## Verify, always

Here is the discipline that keeps you safe. **AI gives hypotheses, not gospel.** It can confidently invent the meaning of an error code that does not exist. So validate every code and claim against **official Microsoft Learn docs** and confirm the actual state in the **portal and logs** before you act. Cross-check the IME log against what the AI claimed. And never paste secrets, tokens, or user PII into a public LLM — strip identifiers first. The AI narrows your search; the evidence closes the case.

## Your task

Pick a real or simulated endpoint issue (an app that won't install or a device gone non-compliant). Collect the error code and one log excerpt, write a structured prompt asking for ranked hypotheses, then validate the top hypothesis in the Intune portal or against Microsoft Learn. Write down which hypothesis was correct and how you confirmed it.

Enrollment failures, devices that won't sync, compliance going red, apps that won't install, cryptic hex error codes. We'll build a repeatable loop with AI as your thinking partner. And as always, AI gives hypotheses, not gospel. You verify everything. Let's go.

Third, ask for ranked hypotheses and the single next diagnostic step, not a magic fix. Fourth, validate against the portal and Microsoft Learn. Round and round until it's solved. AI speeds the loop up, but you are the one closing the case.

For app and script failures, the IntuneManagementExtension log is your goldmine. And note the device's compliance and sync state in Intune. The moment a vague it won't enroll becomes an error code plus log lines, it's a solvable problem.

Notice this prompt: it states the platform, the error, and the environment, then asks for four ranked causes, the one thing to check for each, and the first step. The killer line is the last one, note any cause you are unsure about. That nudges the model to flag its own uncertainty instead of bluffing. Specific context in, ranked investigation plan out.

1. Go to https://intune.microsoft.com
2. Devices > pick the affected device
3. Open the Copilot pane and ask:
   "Why is this device non-compliant and what policy is failing?"
   "When did this device last check in, and is it syncing?"
slides.narration: For anything tenant-specific, Copilot in Intune beats a public chatbot hands down, because it reads your real data. Open the affected device, open the Copilot pane, and ask in plain English why it's non-compliant and which policy is failing, or when it last checked in. The answer is grounded in your actual tenant, not internet guesswork. This is how you confirm device state fast.

slides.title: Common problems AI helps with
bullets: Enrollment failures: licensing, scope, device limits, hybrid trust.
Sync stalls: the device simply hasn't checked in yet.
Compliance red: one setting flips it, triggering CA lockouts.
App install failures: detection rules and dependencies in the IME log.
slides.narration: Here are the usual suspects. Enrollment failures often come down to licensing, auto-enrollment scope, device limits, or hybrid-join trust. Sync stalls are sneaky, the device just hasn't talked to Intune, so policies look unapplied because nothing's run yet. Compliance going red is usually one setting, BitLocker, Defender, OS version, and that can cascade into a Conditional Access lockout. And app failures almost always have their real reason buried in the IME log. AI helps you read all of these faster.

slides.title: Verify, always
bullets: AI gives hypotheses, not gospel.
It can invent the meaning of error codes that don't exist.
Validate every code against official Microsoft Learn docs.
Confirm real state in the portal and logs; strip PII from prompts.
slides.narration: This is the non-negotiable slide. AI gives you hypotheses, not gospel. It will confidently tell you what an error code means, and sometimes that meaning is pure fiction. So validate every code and claim against official Microsoft Learn docs, and confirm the real state in the portal and the logs before you touch anything. Cross-check the IME log against what the AI told you. And strip out secrets and user PII before pasting into any public model. The AI narrows the search; the evidence closes the case.

slides.title: Handle security lockouts with care
bullets: BitLocker and Conditional Access lockouts are sensitive.
AI helps you read the policy chain.
Never bypass a security control on a hunch.
Escalate when access or encryption is involved.
slides.narration: A quick but important word on security lockouts. When BitLocker or Conditional Access is involved, slow down. AI is genuinely useful for tracing the policy chain and explaining which control is blocking access. But you never bypass a security control on a hunch from a chatbot. If access or encryption keys are on the line, follow your escalation process and loop in the right people. AI informs the decision, it doesn't make it for you.
